properties.name: The reasoning read-back keeps the words of every claim it returns, and pages instead of blanking the proof
properties.statement:
When reasoning_report's reply would pass its budget, it returns FEWER claims WHOLE, never every claim with its prose blanked. Each claim it returns carries:
- its statement;
- each supporting step's rule and warrant;
- each premise's name.
The reply says how many claims are left and gives `next_offset` (or an equivalent) to read on, in proof order from the claim asked about.
A budget_chars the server lowers is reported as lowered, naming the cap, never silently.
A capped walk never reports `rests_on: []` or `stated_foundations: []` as if the claim rested on nothing: an unwalked part says it was not walked.
Measured case to carry over: proof-trial rung 2's read-back on design bbcd344a71ff1cbd. All 169 prose fields came back as "…"; budget_chars 120000 was lowered to about 29k with no notice; 25 of 66 claims came back; and the proof was readable only through scan_nodes Inference.
